question: In the sodium chlorate droplet experiments, which saturated salt solution set the humidity at which single crystals were most frequent?
expect: sodium bromide: single crystals become more frequent at RH about 59%, which saturated NaBr maintained (LiCl 11%, MgCl2 33%) (Experimental Setup; Results)
rendered: According to the text, at higher humidity (RH ≈ 59%), the fraction of single-crystal deposits increases, indicating that slower evaporation favors crystal growth within the droplet. The saturated solution of sodium bromide was used to maintain the relative humidity in the capped glass container at 59%.
